question: On 30 October 2020, Samos was hit by a powerful earthquake that caused injuries and significant material damage to houses and shops. Greece is hit by natural disasters often and the absence of civil protection planning is, sadly, accompanied by a lack of care for those affected.

On 21 December 2020, Commissioner Ferreira stated that the European Regional Development Fund can support measures for risk prevention and management, including for systems aimed at disaster management and building disaster resilience.

She added that in the period 2014-2020, EUR 300 million was earmarked for Greek programmes funded by the European Regional Development Fund and the Cohesion Fund for measures to boost civil protection and the prevention and mitigation of natural disasters, such as earthquakes. She said it was up to Member States to plan, choose and implement the co-funded projects.

Unfortunately, the situation thus far is as follows: – three and a half years on, the government has still not fulfilled its promises; – there are 520 building permits yet to be issued for repairs; – no subsidies are given for demolitions; – even the meagre rent subsidy that was being given, stopped 14 months ago. In view of this: 1.
Does the Commission know whether a comprehensive plan (assuming there is one) is being implemented, with a clear timeline for the full reconstruction of the earthquake-affected areas of Samos?
Does it not believe that the reconstruction of areas affected by natural disasters should happen within a set period of time?
Does it not consider that, in the case of Samos, there have been inexplicable and unreasonable delays?
answer: 1. With regards to the European Structural Funds, Member States, in line with the principles of shared management and subsidiarity, remain responsible for the implementation of co-financed actions including project selection.

While the primary responsibility for prevention and coordination of actions in the event of a disaster lies with Member States, the Commission supports national efforts, including with financial resources and economic support. In particular, the 20212027 Cohesion Policy programmes of Greece allocate an amount of EUR 1.46 billion for climate related risk prevention and management.

Moreover, under the programming period 2014-2020, support to Small Medium-sized Enterprises affected by the earthquake was possible under the operational programme ‘Entrepreneurship, Competitiveness, Innovation’. 2. In June 2021, Greece was granted a financial contribution from the EU Solidarity Fund (EUSF) of EUR 2.

5 million to support emergency and recovery operations in the aftermath of the earthquake on the islands of Samos, Ikaria, and Chios in October 2020. Greece indicated that the assistance will be used for the recovery of essential infrastructure, provision of temporary accommodation to the population, cleaning-up operations, and protection of cultural heritage. 3.

According to the EUSF Regulation (1), beneficiary states have 18 months to implement the received financial contribution. In November 2023, Greece submitted an implementation report and statement of validity detailing the use of the financial contribution, and the Commission is currently assessing these documents.
